definition: In learning research, an unconditioned stimulus is the event used to produce a fear reaction without prior training. Changing its intensity or value after learning can alter later fear-related responses during extinction.

reasons: The packet supports that unconditioned stimulus revaluation can affect conditioned fear extinction after acquisition, but it does not explicitly define an unconditioned stimulus as the event used to produce a fear reaction without prior training.
The first sentence adds a general definitional claim that goes beyond the source text and is not directly supported there.

The packet does not define an “unconditioned stimulus” as “the event used to produce a fear reaction without prior training.” It only mentions that the study uses unconditioned stimulus intensity changes within a retrieval-extinction paradigm.

While the packet supports that changing the unconditioned stimulus after acquisition (decreasing its intensity) altered later fear-related outcomes during the extinction/retrieval-extinction stages (e.g., smaller skin conductance responses and different conditioned stimulus pleasure), it does not support the full phrasing of the definition as written.
